reason: Spinu et al. review qAOP models as computational tools that use in vitro and other data to support toxicity prediction and assessment, which fits the cited point about AOP applications for translating toxicity predictions from NAMs.
The cited paper states that its 167 consultant respondents may represent one-quarter of UK NHS neonatal consultants, which matches the claim of around 25%.
The cited paper is a qualitative study of life impacts after ankle fracture and does not address functional bracing or the degree of mechanical support to healing bone.
The citation marks the CLARITY method itself, and the paper describes the simplified CLARITY method (SCM) for tissue clearing.

The protocol only notes prior reports of a therapeutic effect and separate evidence of herbal antimicrobial activity while stressing that no systematic assessment of efficacy yet exists, so the claim that studies show regimens can mitigate SIBO is broadly related but overstated in strength.

The citation credits SOAPnuke as the MapReduce-accelerated software used to filter/preprocess sequencing reads, which the paper describes; the listed options are the authors' run settings, not a claim the paper reports those values.

The review states that TDLN initiate tumor-specific T-cell priming upon antigen recognition and that tumor-derived factors later render them immune-compromised and permissive to invasion and metastasis.

The paper links smoking to an existing smoker identity, social belonging, and fear of losing group status, not to transforming a young, naïve, conformist identity into a confident, mature, rebellious image that acquires enhanced status.
The cited review explicitly states that EVs/exosomes have a short half-life in circulation.
The cited paper calls post-cardiac-surgery AKI a serious complication linked to higher mortality and morbidity, but it does not report reduced long-term survival.
The cited review only says chronic inflammatory signalling can contribute to cancer, not that most cancers are attributable to long-term chronic inflammatory diseases.

The paper does not report that the 3′ end of β-globin promotes nuclear retention; it treats whole-cDNA retention/degradation as prior knowledge cited to other work and instead shows a coding-sequence element that promotes export.

The review supports branched N-glycans on IGFR promoting signaling and tumour growth via galectin lattices that block endocytosis, but it does not state adhesion destabilization, AKT activation, or IGFLR1.
The cited paper explicitly states China's population exceeds 1.4 billion, which supports the population figure this citation plausibly covers; the nurse count is a separate point.
This hospitalized cohort reports 28% mortality (≥20%) and 18.5% ICU admission (within 17–32%), so it supports the overall-mortality and ICU-admission figures it is cited for.

The excerpts link a suitable Cu(I)/Cu(0) ratio to C2 performance but do not mention subsurface oxygen, synergistic Cu+/Cu0 interaction, or a lower C–C coupling energy barrier, which could be discussed elsewhere.

The cited paper is a detailed comparison of absorbed-dose calculation procedures (sVOI, aVOI, and tVOI) for 177Lu-DOTATATE therapy, so it supports citing it as a prior detailed description of that procedure.
The cited paper studies ICT use and economic growth and does not address visual communication tools, SLM, or illiteracy.
The excerpts discuss bacterial NHEJ in some prokaryotes and that DSBs can cause cell death, but none state that E. coli lacks NHEJ or that DSBs are lethal in E. coli for that reason.
The cited abstract states the same point: oral bisphosphonate use in older people is limited by side effects and administration, compromising persistent use.
The cited paper studies vanA transfer in fermented soybean meal and pig feces and never describes pork collection from slaughterhouses or the stated packing, freezing, and 2 h transfer protocol.
The cited paper reports that SFP1 deletion makes C. albicans resistant to cell wall-disrupting agents and to caspofungin, not sensitive to disruptive agents.
The cited paper used six diverse ML algorithms to build and evaluate lymph-node-metastasis models and selected XGBoost after comparing performance.
The review supports flexible, timescale-independent access for e-learning generally, but does not specifically establish asynchronous online learning or call that a unique advantage.
The cited paper's conclusions report the same three social-media factors as associated with greater likelihood of considering future cosmetic procedures.
The review discusses TCR repertoire studies in malignancy, autoimmunity, infectious disease, and aging, supporting the background claim that repertoires are studied in those areas.

The cited paper compares LMM and SEM for mediated longitudinal data and does not justify using LMM instead of SEM because the variables are longitudinal; it treats SEM as preferable for modeling mediation and finds LMM adequate mainly for total effects when the mediator is excluded.
The cited paper reports that compressive strength rises significantly as strain rate increases, supporting the claimed similarity.

The review supports anodal tDCS as a promising way to enhance cognition and slow age-related decline, but it is cautious and mixed, and does not show it is especially effective when coupled with other nonpharmacological interventions.

Vikmoen et al. report that heavy strength training increased patellar tendon CSA in female endurance athletes, supporting the cited claim of PT morphological adaptation; the >6% figure is attributed to Dalgaard, not this paper.
The excerpts discuss multiple barriers to TB treatment adherence but never mention stigma, so they neither support nor contradict the claim.
The cited paper proposes StackedEnC-AOP as a stacked-ensemble method to classify antioxidant proteins and describes encoding via DWT on an evolutionary matrix plus physiochemical descriptors.

The cited paper is about tumor deposits and their effect on metastasis and staging, not evidence that the number and location of metastatic lymph nodes determine clinical staging and treatment planning.

The review supports pandemic-related anxiety and depression in early literature from a few countries, but it does not show comparative increased rates internationally and cautions that findings may not generalize.

The cited paper shows that ICOS pathway blockade in salivary-gland organ cultures reduces IL-21 and inflammatory cytokines and identifies ICOS as a key driver of pathogenic Tfh/Tph and B-cell responses in SS.

The cited paper is a commentary on observational evidence for distancing and PPE that merely mentions existing WHO guidance; it is not a WHO guideline document and does not support development of the survey questions in accordance with such guidelines.

The cited paper states that the Malay Peninsula is the economically more developed and more populous half of Malaysia relative to Sabah and Sarawak, which supports the regional socioeconomic and population contrast attributed to it.

The review defines spliceosomal backsplicing as joining a downstream 5′ splice site to an upstream 3′ splice site and states that a backsplice can force remaining pre-mRNA to splice alternatively or be degraded.

The cited paper only describes fieldmap/EPI distortion correction, phase unwrapping, eddy-current correction and head-motion correction, not the claimed pipeline of DWI denoising, Gibbs ringing correction and bias-field correction.
The cited paper links antioxidant and FRAP differences to extracting solvent, not to plant parts, harvesting time, or geoclimatic conditions.
The cited paper explicitly reports developing IPTG-inducible Pgrac100-based vectors that give high recombinant protein production in B. subtilis and relatively low basal expression in E. coli.

The citing text lists this paper as a cohort study, but the excerpts show a laboratory study of CHIKV in mouse, monkey, and human saliva that only used some samples from an existing cohort, not a cohort study itself.
The excerpts never report an attrition or dropout rate, so they do not show whether intervention-phase attrition in this trial was higher than in the citing study.

The paper links childhood abuse to MAYSI-2 self-report problems in a small detained JSO sample and reports no JSO vs non-JSO difference; it does not find that up to two-thirds of juvenile sex offenders meet diagnostic criteria or show remarkable psychopathology.
The paper uses the tetraspanin CD63 as an exosomal marker to characterize/recognize exosomes, supporting the general claim.

The cited study compares wild and long-colonized An. stephensi fed P. vivax and frames higher wild-mosquito sporozoite loads as a reason for caution that colonization-associated genetic change may alter vector susceptibility.
The cited paper directly reports a measurable, sequence-dependent difference in cellular uptake kinetics between two siRNA sequences.

The cited paper states that FIFA 11+ has been shown in several studies to reduce amateur football injuries and summarizes long-term worldwide dissemination of the programme, supporting both points attached to the citation.
The cited paper explicitly states that its aim is to estimate the contribution of human-to-human transmission to the Lassa fever burden among cases in Sierra Leone.
The paper finds only minimal extra spectral information for H&E nuclear classification and calls the benefit largely unknown, but it does not report discrepancies among previous studies.
The paper supports a critical anti-tumour role for cDC1, but it is a mouse cDC1-subset study and does not show conserved roles of activated cDC subsets.

The paper lists strengthening governance and leadership among emerging ingredients to explore for health sector reforms, but does not call leadership a key ingredient specifically for healthcare reform in low-income settings.

Lawson et al. 2020 reports building a more comprehensive zebrafish transcriptome annotation that addresses deficiencies in existing annotations, supporting the claim that zebrafish genome annotations continue to be improved.
The cited paper links HaHSFA4a and HaHSFA9 to desiccation and severe dehydration tolerance, which supports the claim that HsfA4 and HsfA9 are related to drought resistance.

The paper notes that music therapy is a cost-effective, lower-risk non-pharmacological option with broad clinical value amid growing research, but it does not state that fewer side effects, lower costs, and greater safety have increasingly captured clinical practitioners’ interest.
The paper does say regular HIV-1 evolution/RT cannot be formally excluded, but it reports mutations clustering at the Cas9 cleavage site (one PAM exception), not substitutions further away.
The cited paper reports that purified HPV18 His6-E6, like HPV16, degrades MAGI-3 in vitro, supporting the claim that HPV18 E6 can degrade MAGI3 protein.

The citation is attached to a claim that CSFP patients may present with fragmented QRS complexes, but the cited paper only reports higher P-wave and QT-interval dispersion in slow coronary flow and does not mention fragmented QRS.
DESeq2 is a count-based differential-expression method and the paper’s calling example uses adjusted P < 0.1, not FPKM equated with fold-change ≥1.00 and adjusted p ≤ 0.05.

The paper defines PDR as stride-wise updates of stride length and heading with growing drift, not continuous velocity/orientation estimation that yields a stable position (that continuous integration is what it attributes to SINS).
The cited review explicitly states there are few data suggesting harm from β-blockers and that patients should not be denied them if required.
The paper supports high-fidelity simulation to assess EPA 10 and entrustment, but it does not show correlation with entrustment in clinical settings.
The cited paper is the MetaboAnalyst tool description and explicitly includes heatmap visualization, supporting its use to generate heatmaps.

The cited review states that the S glycoprotein has S1 and S2 subunits, with S1 containing the receptor-binding domain that governs host-cell tropism and S2 mediating membrane fusion, matching the cited claim.
The cited case report found B. henselae DNA in all 11 feeding Ixodes ricinus ticks removed from a cat that was seropositive for anti-B. henselae IgG, which supports the cited demonstration.
The cited paper explicitly identifies BS-181 as a selective/specific CDK7 inhibitor and reports IC50 values showing much stronger inhibition of CDK7 than other CDKs.
